license_note: The model card links its license to Google's Gemma 4 license page, which carries the Apache License 2.0 text in full, and Google's own release blog states the weights are "Released under an Apache 2.0 license". The Gemma Terms of Use, whose appendix does not list DiffusionGemma, state that Gemma 4 terms are in the separate Gemma 4 license, so the Gemma Terms of Use use restrictions and the incorporated Gemma Prohibited Use Policy do not attach to this release. No LICENSE file ships in the repository, so the grant rests on the card metadata and the linked license page.

access_boundary: This record represents the google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it weight release published on Hugging Face at commit f7f5b7f5fa82ffc52addd066915886d497f5517b, the instruction-tuned 26B-total, 3.8B-active DiffusionGemma checkpoint. The Gemma 4 26B A4B autoregressive base it is fine-tuned from, the Diffusion Explained sample application, the community FP8 and 4-bit quantizations and the 31 finetune derivatives, and the Vertex AI Model Garden deployment of the same weights are separate boundaries.
strengths: Ungated Apache-2.0 weights in an official Google Hugging Face organization, with the full Apache 2.0 text linked from the model card and the release blog

First open-weights Google release built on discrete text diffusion rather than autoregression, documented end to end by a separate Diffusion Explained page covering Uniform State Diffusion, incremental prefill, and denoising

First-party model card publishes the architecture table, 256-token canvas, 1024-token sliding window, 8-of-128 expert routing, recommended sampler settings, per-runtime deployment commands, a training-data description with a January 2025 cutoff, and a safety evaluation section
Served from Google's own Vertex AI Model Garden, which the developer documentation links directly from the model overview
tradeoffs: Google documents the release as experimental, and its own comparison table shows it scoring below the Gemma 4 base it derives from on most text and vision benchmarks

Google states the parallel-decoding advantage is aimed at low-concurrency single-user local use and diminishes under high-QPS cloud workloads, so the throughput case does not transfer to server deployments
No LICENSE file ships in the repository, so the grant rests on the card metadata and the linked license page rather than an in-repo license artifact
No deprecation or versioning posture is published for the line, and the repository's last commit is 15 July 2026
